purpose: Bind MCP usage into the SEIS full-usage operating mode so future Design, Developer, DevOps, Coding, LLM, Software Engineering, and AI work can use the repo-owned SEIS MCP server first, then approved external MCPs only through explicit risk, credential, and evidence gates.
truthBoundary: MCP binding means the repo-owned SEIS MCP server is available as a local, public-safe, stdio resource and tool surface for future full-usage work. It does not prove authenticated external MCP access, cloud provider access, browser-session safety, package-runner safety, SSH, deployment, GitHub mutation, billing actions, or credential readiness.

mcpUseOrder.use: Use the repo-owned local SEIS MCP server for source-of-truth resources, status tools, and bounded checks.
Read public-safe SEIS resources for provider registry, MCP binding, subagent ledgers, model boundaries, and governance contracts.
Use bounded local check tools only when their scope is explicit and command output is recorded.
Render public-safe prompts for repeatable review without embedding private conversation dumps or credentials.
Use installed external MCPs only after server identity, permissions, auth boundary, failure behavior, and owner scope are recorded.
Keep candidate MCPs as research or documentation-only entries until reviewed.
Block external writes, sends, schedules, deploys, deletes, issue updates, database writes, and repo mutations until an explicit owner-approved runbook exists.

domainBindings.safeUse: Read design-system contracts, render review prompts, and collect visual QA status without external design-tool mutation.
Inspect workspace state, read source-of-truth records, and run bounded local checks with Codex as the single writer.
Read cloud, SSH, release, and readiness contracts without deployment, SSH execution, or provider mutation.
Use MCP checks and prompts as scoped helpers while repository edits remain in Codex.
Read provider, model-router, prompt, and retention contracts before any helper/model route decision.
Use architecture, testing, security, performance, and maintainability checks as evidence surfaces.
Read AI Core, provider registry, MCP permissioning, sub-agent, and model-boundary resources without live provider calls.

observedRisks: runtime dependencies are installed into a user-home runtime directory
native or optional runtime dependencies may be lazy-installed on macOS or Linux
package acts as a local CLI/server/proxy surface
source repository was not declared in the observed npm metadata
installGate: explicit owner approval for package-runner install
tarball or source review before execution
no credentials available during install or first run
rollback command and runtime directory cleanup plan
repo-only result ledger after any action

eligibleWhen: mutation scope is absent or explicitly approved

forbiddenWithoutExplicitOwnerApproval: browser automation on authenticated private pages
completionDefinition: The repo-owned `seis` MCP server is present in `.mcp.json`.
The full-usage MCP binding is exposed as `seis://ai/full-usage-mcp-binding.json`.
The MCP runtime contract, permission matrix, smoke test, docs, and checker script agree on 35 tools, 33 resources, and 3 prompts.
External MCPs remain candidate, verified-task-scoped, or blocked according to the permission risk matrix.
No credential, provider-call, external-mutation, SSH, deploy, billing, or GitHub mutation claim is made without separate evidence.
nextSafeActions: Use `seis://ai/full-usage-mcp-binding.json` as the first MCP context resource before future MCP-assisted work.
Create a per-use MCP ledger before allowing external MCP output to shape repository decisions.
Keep credentialed and mutation-capable MCPs owner-action gated until a target-specific runbook exists.
